properties.name: REPRODUCED: two exports between commits sever the lineage chain and turn the design gate RED — the collision is real, not an artifact of committing. And the hypothesis that 'no commit, no push' avoids it is FALSIFIED, because the chain is built from the FILE, not from git
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at main `8ba3198`, deliberately falsifying an agent hypothesis rather than confirming it.

═══ THE HYPOTHESIS THAT WAS WRONG ═══

The agent proposed that `dec:idea-does-the-graph-write-itself-through-to-the-repo-on-every-change`'s unresolved collision might be ILLUSORY, reasoning: the proposal is *"no commit, no push"*, `dec:export-once-per-PR` is a rule about COMMITS, and a working-tree file that is never committed cannot violate a rule about commits.

❌ **FALSIFIED.** The chain is built from **the file already at the target path**, not from git. Writing that file twice between commits chains the second export through an intermediate that will never enter history — whether or not anything is committed in between.

═══ THE REPRODUCTION ═══

One graph write, export, one more graph write (a single AUTHORED_BY edge), export again — then run the gate against the working file:

    committed hash   sha256:29d103c800e9...
    working prev     sha256:00255feac6d8...   <- the intermediate, never committed
    working hash     sha256:7b4e7b2c4ee1...

    FAIL  LINEAGE  'docs/design/reflow2.json' does not link to the export it
                   replaced: it records 00255fea... where 29d103c8... is expected.
    reflow2 check: FAILED — 1 finding(s), 10 note(s).

This is exactly cause (2) named in `reflow2_check`'s own message: *"The design was exported MORE THAN ONCE since the last commit, chaining through an intermediate that will never be committed."* ⇒ **AUTO-EXPORT ON EVERY CHANGE, WRITING TO THE COMMITTED PATH, TURNS THE DESIGN GATE RED ON EVERY BRANCH.** The blocker is real and it is not about discipline; it is arithmetic on a hash chain.

The documented fix works and was confirmed: `git checkout <path>` then export ONCE — the gate returns to OK.

═══ ⭐⭐ AND THE SAME EXPERIMENT NAMES THE WAY OUT ═══

The chain breaks only because the durability write and the archival write TARGET THE SAME PATH. They are different acts with different audiences — one is "do not lose this", the other is "this is the record of the branch" — and nothing requires them to share a file.

**Auto-export to a SEPARATE path** (`.reflow2/<graph>.autosave.json`, gitignored) and the collision disappears entirely: the committed export keeps its one-per-PR chain untouched, while the durable copy is refreshed as often as anybody likes. Measured cost of a save: **265 ms**. No change to the lineage rule, no git awareness in the core, and `dec:export-once-per-pr` stays exactly as written.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether a gitignored autosave is a good enough durable copy to hang the inversion on — it is not in version control, so it survives a crash but not a lost working tree. That is the same question `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` asks, and this only removes the lineage objection from it.

⚠️ BOUNDS: one design, one path, one machine, debug binary. The gate was exercised in its pre-commit form (working file vs HEAD); the CI form (HEAD vs HEAD~1) was not separately reproduced, though `_export_pair` states both use one rule.
